sources.entry: PHP: _Write your own MVC from scratch in PHP_

summary.title: Write your own MVC from scratch in PHP
summary.one_liner: You learn how the Model-View-Controller pattern works and how to build a minimal URL-routed MVC framework in PHP in under 300 lines.
takeaways: MVC splits an app into Model (database access), View (presentation) and Controller (logic and request handling).
A single index.php entry point can route URLs of the form /Controller/function/args to controller methods.
call_user_func_array(array(new $controller, $method), $args) invokes a controller method with URL arguments.
Appending the HTTP method name (e.g. hello_get, hello_post) to the function name separates GET and POST handling.
A base CJ_Model wraps a mysqli connection with create, read, update, delete and where helpers, and a load_view helper extracts variables into a plain PHP view file.
summary.summary: The article explains the MVC pattern and then builds a small PHP MVC framework step by step. It covers a directory layout (config, controller, core, model, view), a single index.php entry point that parses the URL to find a controller and method, and dispatches via call_user_func_array. Method names get a _get or _post suffix based on the request method. The base model class connects to MySQL through mysqli with CRUD helpers, and a load_view function passes variables into a plain PHP template. The code is shown inline and the full source is linked to GitHub.
